target_customer: Auto shops and centralized maintenance facilities for rental, delivery, trucking, transit, municipal and refuse fleets
problem: Fleet shops lack technician capacity for routine inspections, fluids, electronics and tires.
business_model: Robots plus maintenance intelligence software sold to shops; pricing not public

founders.name: Michael Hazard
education: Stanford, Computer Science with AI focus

founders.name: Colby Duke
education: Georgia Tech, Computer Science with AI and Robotics focus

technical_complexity.rationale: General purpose robotic servicing across vehicle models with fluids, electronics and tires is hard; company reports 96% autonomy on initial tasks.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware plus shop software integrations are hard to copy quickly, but tire robot rivals are already funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to know; no incumbent move found.

market_need_then: Technician shortages and growing fleets, including robotaxis, strain maintenance capacity.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and practical: 'Machines that keep machines running.'

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable real word name but a branding search found no brand press or community.

outcome_analysis: Rodeo Robotics is a two person Fall 2026 YC company from ex Applied Intuition founders building maintenance robots for fleets, with customer deployments planned for January 2027. No financing or outcome is public. Hardware difficulty and funded tire robot rivals are the main uncertainties.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k Seed (single aggregator, unverified, not recorded). The 96% autonomy figure and deployment date are company stated. PitPro (Sept 2026) postdates founding and is omitted. Competitors are dated from 2026 coverage; RoboTire's Series A is older and its date was not in the snippet. Completeness pass: the 125K seed rests on a single database (Dealroom), with no date given.
